briefings.1: Reserve perimeter breached east of the river. Wildlife counts off by four hundred percent. Nothing inside the wall grew that fast on the catalogue. The biology team is not sleeping.
briefings.2: Pack behaviour cleaner than instinct. They flanked the second wave the way the manual flanks them. Watching the lab tape on loop. Nobody on the team will sign off on the word coincidence.
briefings.3: Lost two forward outposts overnight. Silhouettes on the thermals larger than anything that came out of our tanks. Three weeks ago they were that size on paper only. They are growing between encounters.
briefings.4: Containment line failed at the marsh. The fall-back is now official. The animals on the other side of the river are not the species we revived nine years ago. We are still trying to call them by those names.
briefings.5: Smoke north of the ridge. Something the size of a building moves through it and is not afraid of fire. Designate her Matriarch. The catalogue does not have an entry. We are writing one in pencil.
briefings.6: Forced north. The cold should slow them. It does not. The lab measured a corpse this morning — the integument has thickened in the time it took us to retreat. They are adapting between contact and contact.
briefings.7: Tracks across the snow are wrong. Too heavy. Too many. The line of advance is too straight to be a migration. The thing that is doing this is not behaving like an animal and we have no word for the alternative.
briefings.8: Two corridors out of the pass and both compromised. The herd splits itself to flank us, on time, without any signal we can intercept. Whatever is coordinating them is inside them now.
briefings.9: Specimens recovered from the tar are decades-old normals. What is hunting us now grew last quarter. Same species on paper. Not the same animal. The lab cannot tell us what changed because the change is still happening.
briefings.10: Larger frame, denser bone. They are bigger between encounters than they should be. Matriarch sighted again — she brought a herd that did not exist last month. The herd is making more of itself faster than we can count.
briefings.11: Integument now deflects kinetic rounds at range. Cross-section shows our scaffolding alloy threaded through the dermal layers. They are growing the metal into themselves. The metal is keeping pace.
briefings.12: Confirmed: the larger specimens arrive plated. Both lane entries breached. Whatever round we ended last week with, next week's wave is wearing it. We are watching evolution happen on the firing line.
briefings.13: Smaller specimens healing the larger ones mid-engagement. Wounds closing as we watch. The revival tanks did this for us once under sterile conditions. The animals are doing it to each other in the open. We did not design that.
briefings.14: Wounds open and close again before the next volley. Regenerating in real time, on every casualty we inflict. We taught the tanks to do this. Nobody taught the animals. They learned it off our own equipment growing inside them.
briefings.15: Dossier 14-A: a single specimen leads them. She does not run. The pack does not run while she is present. The Matriarch returns. The biology team has stopped going to bed. We have stopped pretending this stops.
briefings.16: Past the last city. There has not been a city for some time. The maps in the operator pack are no longer accurate to the landscape they describe. The landscape has stopped being the landscape we surveyed.
briefings.17: Operator: count the silhouettes on the ridge before you report how many we are killing. The difference between those numbers is the species we are losing to. The kills are not the war. The kills are how we are buying hours.
briefings.18: The fortified specimens we are calling reefs. They do not break. They only stop. Each one we cannot remove is one approach lane the herd now owns. They are investing in geography. We are running out of geography.
briefings.19: Three approach lanes synchronised this morning. No signal between them on any band we monitor. They are no longer transmitting because they no longer need to. Whatever the lattice grew into them is doing the talking.
briefings.20: Ninth day with no civilian transmission on any frequency. Ground cover dying out to thirty kilometres around the cordon. Native fauna gone from the survey grid. The Extinction Protocol is the only directive still being repeated.
briefings.21: The continent is venting along their migration corridors. They walk through the magma. The integument does not burn. The vents were not there last quarter. The ground is changing to suit them, not us.
briefings.22: Forward observers report the larger specimens are actively hunting us. Two scouts came back to the perimeter. Placed. We were not the prey in any of the original studies. The studies are no longer the studies they were.
briefings.23: Ground readings inconsistent with biology. Something the size of a building stood here this morning long enough to dent the basalt. It is not here now. It is ahead of us, between us and the basin.
briefings.24: Each wave is heavier than the last by an order we cannot graph. Recommended evacuation. Evacuation denied — there is no rear line. The ground behind us is no longer the ground we walked in on.
briefings.25: Last ridge before the basin. South of this position the soil chemistry is no longer the soil chemistry of this planet. North of this position there is nothing left for the convoy to fall back to. The map ends here.
briefings.26: The ground is no longer ours. Instruments do not parse the chemistry underfoot. The plants are not plants. The herd metabolises what grows here. We do not. The air at the cordon is failing the reference scale.
briefings.27: They no longer bleed the right colour. The casualty form still has a column for blood type. We have stopped filling it in. There is no equivalent on the chart for what comes out of these animals now.
briefings.28: Counts are no longer meaningful. New phenotypes between every wave. The animal we killed this morning is not what arrives this evening. The catalogue is closed. The line still has to hold.
briefings.29: Quiet for nine minutes. The biome is still spreading underneath us. Whatever the herd is assembling next, it does not need us to see it to finish. The silence is not peace. It is preparation.
briefings.30: The Matriarch is here. She is what the programme made when it would not stop. The biosphere is hers. The Protocol was always for her. There is nothing else left to do. Engage.

interstitials.1: Day one. Kairos Corp has been running the revival programme at industrial scale for nine years. Seventy-two hours ago the reserve perimeter failed and the specimens that walked out were larger, denser, and more coordinated than any catalogue entry the programme has ever produced. The cloning vats inside the wall are still running; shutdown of the rigs requires a corporate signature nobody has produced. Operator role: hold the outpost ring while local population evacuates east. Every emplacement that holds is hours bought for the convoy. We are not retaking ground.
interstitials.2: The evacuation east of the river is still moving in numbers, and most of the column does not yet know the wall will not be rebuilt. Pack behaviour on the inbound waves is reading cleaner than instinct — coordinated flanking that matches our own containment doctrine, turned back against the line. The conditioning hardware inside the reserve was built to teach revived specimens to move as a managed population, and that programme did not stop when the perimeter came down. Every emplacement that holds the ring keeps the river crossing open another few hours. The line is covering an evacuation, not retaking ground.
interstitials.3: Two forward outposts went dark overnight — no contact, no bodies recovered. Thermal silhouettes on the approach are larger than anything the revival tanks were rated to produce, and larger this week than last; the specimens are gaining mass between encounters, not across generations. That growth profile matches the reserve's accelerated-maturation rigs, which means the rigs are still feeding the population now on the wrong side of the river. Corporate command on the coast keeps issuing perimeter-repair orders into a chain the open ground is already pulling apart. Hold the crossing; the column has not finished moving.
interstitials.4: Containment failed at the marsh, and the fall-back is now the standing posture rather than a contingency. The animals across the river are no longer the species revived nine years ago — the catalogue names still printed on the casualty forms describe a population that no longer exists. The revival rigs cannot be shut down: the cloning vats and the conditioning lattice inside the wall need a corporate signature, and command on the coast has not produced one. What was an orderly evacuation is now a refugee movement under operator escort. Hold each outpost long enough for the column to clear the next.
interstitials.5: A single apex specimen has been sighted north of the ridge — larger than any tank output, moving through smoke and fire that should have turned it. Designate her Matriarch; the catalogue has no entry, and the biology team is writing one from observation alone. The herd does not scatter while she holds the field, which is conditioning-network behaviour rather than anything wild. As of this sighting corporate command has privately stopped planning to rebuild the wall, though no order to that effect will be issued. Hold the ridge; the forest is the last band where the map still matches the ground.
interstitials.6: Coastal cordon fell on day six. Climate gradient was projected as a hard ceiling on specimen movement — it has not been. Tissue samples from the leading edge show our scaffolding alloy laminated into the integument; the animals are not carrying the hardware, they are made of it, and the metal is keeping them warm. Civilian convoy is now north of the treeline and moving. Every ridge we hold buys time for the column to dig in at the next ridge. The line is not advancing. The line is buying hours.
interstitials.7: The coastal cordon is gone, and the column is north of the treeline in country that was never provisioned for it. Tracks across the snow run too heavy and too straight to read as migration — the leading edge is advancing on a line, not foraging. The cold was projected as a hard ceiling on specimen movement and has held nothing; tissue off the dead shows the integument thickening between contacts to hold heat. Whatever is setting that line of advance is not behaving as an animal, and the station has no working word for the alternative. Hold the pass; each ridge bought is dig-in time for the column at the next.
interstitials.8: Both corridors out of the pass are compromised, and the herd is splitting itself to take them at once — on time, with no transmission on any band we monitor. The coordination is running inside the animals now, on neural tissue grown out of the conditioning lattice, so there is no signal to intercept and nothing to jam. Six weeks of attrition has not net-reduced the population; the rigs inside the reserve still produce faster than emplacements can attrit. The middle layer of corporate command has gone quiet — regional directors out of contact, station chiefs holding on their own authority. Hold both corridors as long as the column needs them.
interstitials.9: Specimens recovered from the tar fields are decades-old normals — ordinary revived stock, the population we catalogued. What is hunting the column now grew last quarter and shares only a name with them. The divergence is the clearest field confirmation yet that the revival hardware never stopped iterating: it is rewriting the animals between engagements faster than any species adapts in a generation. The first internal report saying as much is circulating on station, and there is no longer anyone with the authority to act on it. Hold the tar line; the column is still moving and still exposed.
interstitials.10: A second apex specimen has entered the field, and she did not arrive alone — the herd around her does not appear on any count taken last month. The population is producing reinforcements at revival grade in the open, which means the apex specimens can now trigger the reproduction the rigs were built to run under controlled conditions. By this point the corporate command structure has lost its middle entirely; orders are local, and the chain east to the coast is effectively severed. The mountain passage ahead is the column's only route south, and it is narrowing. Hold the snow line until the column commits to the pass.
interstitials.11: Northern fall-back terminated at the mountains. Convoy diverted south through the high-desert corridor. Specimen morphology on the leading edge no longer matches the catalogue — shielded integument is now the dominant phenotype on inbound waves. Internal review concludes the revival hardware never stopped iterating: it is rewriting the animals between engagements, selecting against the round that killed the last wave faster than any natural species adapts in a generation. Every kill is data; every wave is the species that data produced. We have been training the herd that is eating the continent. The corridor must hold until the column clears.
interstitials.12: Mountain passage failed, and the column has diverted south through the high-desert corridor. Shielded integument is now the dominant phenotype on inbound waves — recovered cross-sections show our scaffolding alloy threaded through the dermal layers, deflecting kinetic rounds at range. The pattern is no longer deniable: each wave wears the round that ended the last one, because the network selects against whatever damage type the line fields. Every kill we log is data the herd integrates against us, which makes winning the engagement the mechanism of the next one's difficulty. Hold the corridor until the column clears; the harder the wave, the closer behind it we have driven the herd.
interstitials.13: Smaller specimens are now closing the wounds of the larger ones mid-engagement, in the open, with no sterile field. The revival tanks ran regeneration like this once under containment; the animals are doing it to each other on the firing line, off conditioning hardware grown into their tissue. This is a response the network produced against the sustained damage the line has delivered for twelve outposts — in effect, we trained the wave that is now un-killing itself in front of us. Suppressing the support specimens before the heavy frames is the only way the line holds. The corridor has to stay open; the column is not yet through the desert.
interstitials.14: Wounds are opening and closing again before the next volley lands — regeneration in real time, on every casualty inflicted. Heal-support alone did not hold against our fire, so the network has pushed the capability into the casualties themselves; this is the loop adapting one step past the counter we found last week. We taught the revival tanks to do this. No one taught the animals — they took it off our own equipment growing inside them, and they are iterating faster than ordnance can keep pace. Hold the corridor, and accept that attrition is now buying the column's hours, not reducing the herd.
interstitials.15: A third apex specimen leads the inbound herd, and the formation does not run while she holds the field — the conditioning-network hypothesis is now the working consensus on station. She does not break, and the herd around her does not break with her; recovered samples place her among the most heavily integrated specimens the programme has produced. The coastal cordon behind us is hours from being overrun, and cities off the coast are going with it, because the herd has stopped migrating along coastlines. The Extinction Protocol, until now a contingency document, is moving toward becoming the only standing order, because no other order is being issued. Hold the desert line; there is no fall-back left that is not already failing.
interstitials.16: Coastal cordon is gone. So is the coast. The remaining civilian population is dispersed across uncatalogued terrain; operators are reaching them by runner, not radio. The herd has stopped behaving like an ecology — they coordinate without signal, breed faster than the rigs ever did inside the wall, and adapt between waves in ways the biology team has stopped trying to predict. The native biosphere between outposts is failing: ground cover dying off, surface water turning, catalogued fauna gone from the survey grids around every emplacement still reporting. The Extinction Protocol is the only standing directive. Tactical-yield ordnance authorised from this point.
interstitials.17: Read the ground before reporting kills: count the silhouettes massing on the ridge against the number put down, and the difference is the species the continent is being lost to. The kills are not the war — they are how the outpost buys hours for a civilian network now reachable by runner, not radio. The herd has stopped behaving as an ecology; it breeds faster than the rigs ever did inside the wall and coordinates without any signal we can find. The native biosphere between emplacements is failing — ground cover dying off, catalogued fauna gone from the survey grids around every position still reporting. Hold the line, and log the gap between kills and silhouettes; that gap is the only honest metric left.
interstitials.18: Fortified specimens — designated reefs — are arriving that do not break under fire. They only stop, and each one that cannot be removed becomes an approach lane the herd owns from then on. The herd is investing in geography, turning our own kill-zones into cover, and the line is running out of ground to trade. This is the collapse phase: the operator net is isolated outposts on isolated emplacements, with no continuous front between them. Hold what geography remains; every lane the reefs take is one the column cannot use either.
interstitials.19: Three approach lanes synchronised their advance this morning with no transmission between them on any band. The herd is not transmitting because it no longer needs to — the conditioning lattice has finished growing into its nervous tissue, and the coordination is running on hardware we built, inside animals we cannot open in time to learn how. This is multi-vector behaviour the network produced after eighteen outposts of processing our lane discipline; the timing is a direct read of how the line has defended every corridor before this one. Splitting fire across all three lanes is the only hold, and it thins each of them. Hold every vector; there is no longer a flank that is not also a front.
interstitials.20: Ninth day with no civilian transmission on any frequency — the native biosphere outside the cordon has failed widely enough that no one is left maintaining the radio infrastructure. Ground cover is dying out to thirty kilometres around the position, and the survey grids are empty of catalogued fauna. The decision to keep the operator net running is now made by station chiefs individually; there is no corporate decision-maker left to make it. The Extinction Protocol is the only directive still being repeated, because it is the only one ever written for a situation with no rear line. Hold the cordon, and understand there is nothing behind it to fall back to.
interstitials.21: Continental interior is no longer recognisable on satellite. Geothermal venting follows herd migration corridors precisely. Atmospheric chemistry is drifting where the densest grazing pressure has been longest. Surveyors are no longer describing this as damage to the landscape. The hardware now grown into the apex specimens appears to be catalysing the change directly — what they walk through, the planet becomes; what they pass over, the native biosphere does not survive. Every emplacement that still holds is one square kilometre that does not become the new biome.
interstitials.22: Forward observers report the larger specimens are hunting our positions rather than advancing through them — two scouts came back to the perimeter placed deliberately, where they would be found. We were not the prey in any of the original revival studies, and the studies no longer describe the animals they were written about. This is the terraforming phase, and the herd can afford to spend effort on us specifically because the population is no longer pressured for numbers. Attrition has stopped meaning anything at the strategic scale; the rigs and the field reproduction together outproduce every emplacement on the line. Hold the position, and assume the line is under study in return.
interstitials.23: Ground readings along the approach are inconsistent with any biology in the catalogue. Something the size of a building stood at this position long enough this morning to dent the basalt, and it is gone now — ahead of us, between the line and the basin we are trying to reach. The apex specimens are reshaping the crust as they pass; geothermal corridors are opening on their paths faster than survey can map them. The basin is the last position from which the original revival site can be engaged, and the herd is moving to close it first. Hold the approach; we are racing the terraform to the only ground that still matters.
interstitials.24: Each wave is now heavier than the last by a margin that will not fit on the same axis as the one before it. Recommended evacuation has been denied at command level — not refused, denied, because there is no rear line to evacuate to and the ground behind the position is no longer the ground we walked in on. The herd is restructuring the planet faster than any emplacement can attrit it, and the late-game population is past the point where killing reduces it in any meaningful sense. What the line holds for now is not territory but the approach to the basin. Hold; the column is what remains here, and there is nowhere to send it.
interstitials.25: This is the last ridge before the basin. South of the position the soil chemistry is no longer the soil chemistry of this planet; north of it there is nothing left for the convoy to fall back to. The new biome is closing around the basin, and once it does the line will be fighting inside the herd's terraform output rather than at its edge. The original revival site sits at the centre of that biome — the apex of everything the programme grew — and the basin is the last ground from which it can still be reached. Hold the ridge; the map ends here, and the only direction left is in.
interstitials.26: The new biome covers approximately one hundred and thirty thousand square kilometres and is still spreading at nine kilometres per day. Ground biology does not match anything in the planetary catalogue. Atmospheric readings inside the zone are off the reference scale; the air at the cordon will not support our respiration much longer. Command considers the planet lost — there is no plan past this directive. Operator role: locate and engage the apex specimen at the original revival site. The Extinction Protocol has not been countermanded because there is nobody left with the authority to countermand it.
interstitials.27: The specimens no longer bleed the colour the casualty form has a column for, and the station has stopped filling that column in. There is no equivalent on any chart for what comes out of these animals now; their metabolism runs on hardware-laced chemistry the planetary catalogue cannot parse. The line is fighting inside the terraform output — violet biocrust, crystallised discharge, plant life no one seeded — and the air at the cordon is failing the reference scale. Command considers the planet lost; there is no plan past the directive that put the operator here. Hold the approach to the revival site; everything outside it already belongs to the herd.
interstitials.28: Counts have stopped being meaningful — new phenotypes arrive between every wave, and the animal killed this morning is not what comes in tonight. The catalogue is formally closed; there is nothing stable left to name. This is the herd's terraform at full output, generating variation faster than observation can record it, off a metabolism built on our own integration hardware. The line still has to hold — not because holding reverses anything, but because the approach to the apex specimen is the only ground action still worth its cost. Hold the position; identification is no longer part of the work.
interstitials.29: Nine minutes of quiet on the approach — no contact, no movement on any sensor. The biome is spreading underneath the position the entire time; whatever the herd is assembling next does not need to be observed to be finished. The silence is not a lull and it is not peace; it reads as the last of the pre-engagement conditioning the network runs before it commits the apex specimen. The original revival site is directly ahead, and everything between here and it has gone still at once. Hold and ready the line; the quiet is preparation, and it is nearly spent.
interstitials.30: The apex specimen is here — at the centre of the new biome, on the ground where the revival programme began. She is what the programme made once no one with the authority to stop it remained: the most heavily integrated specimen it ever produced, bone and lattice and regenerative metabolism grown past anything the tanks could hold. The biosphere is hers now; the planet is the environment she prefers, and we are the invasive species in it. The Extinction Protocol was always written for her, and this engagement is the only ground action that can still meaningfully reduce her. There is no line behind this one and no directive after it. Engage.

verdant.name: Verdant Spiral
verdant.blurb: Forest gauntlet — one long serpentine lane snakes the whole field.

magma.name: Magma Coil
magma.blurb: Volcanic basin — a mirrored coil winds past molten rivers.

hive.name: Hive Labyrinth
hive.blurb: Alien reaches — twin lanes pour in from both flanks.
